// A builtin `hash` value: any JSON value every language holds exactly (null, bool,
// string, number, array, object), with object keys in wire order. The TS codec
// accepts the same set. The XML any-attribute target is the same type; its
// values are strings on read and scalars on write.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct NeutralNumber(String);
impl NeutralNumber {
 // The JSON spelling of a number a double holds exactly: an integer-spelled number
 // inside +-(2^53-1) that is not -0, otherwise a spelling equal to ECMAScript
 // Number::toString of its value ("0.1", "1e+21"; never "1.0", "1e20", "0.10").
 pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, &'static str> {
  let b = s.as_bytes(); let mut i = if b.first() == Some(&b'-') { 1 } else { 0 };
  let digits = |i: &mut usize| { let at = *i; while *i < b.len() && b[*i].is_ascii_digit() { *i += 1; } *i - at };
  let whole = i; let n = digits(&mut i);
  if n == 0 || (n > 1 && b[whole] == b'0') { return Err("not a JSON number"); }
  let mut integer = true;
  if i < b.len() && b[i] == b'.' { integer = false; i += 1; if digits(&mut i) == 0 { return Err("not a JSON number"); } }
  if i < b.len() && (b[i] == b'e' || b[i] == b'E') { integer = false; i += 1; if i < b.len() && (b[i] == b'+' || b[i] == b'-') { i += 1; }
   if digits(&mut i) == 0 { return Err("not a JSON number"); } }
  if i != b.len() { return Err("not a JSON number"); }
  let exact = if integer { s != "-0" && n <= 16 && s.trim_start_matches('-').parse::<u64>().is_ok_and(|v| v <= 9_007_199_254_740_991) }
   else { s.parse::<f64>().is_ok_and(|f| f.is_finite() && Self::es_string(f) == s) };
  if exact { Ok(Self(s.into())) } else { Err("number cannot be held exactly") }
 }
 fn es_string(x: f64) -> String {
  if x == 0.0 { return "0".into(); }
  let sci = format!("{:e}", x.abs()); let (m, e) = sci.split_once('e').unwrap();
  let d: String = m.chars().filter(|c| *c != '.').collect(); let k = d.len() as i32; let n = e.parse::<i32>().unwrap() + 1;
  let sign = if x < 0.0 { "-" } else { "" };
  let body = if k <= n && n <= 21 { format!("{d}{}", "0".repeat((n - k) as usize)) }
   else if 0 < n && n <= 21 { format!("{}.{}", &d[..n as usize], &d[n as usize..]) }
   else if -6 < n && n <= 0 { format!("0.{}{d}", "0".repeat((-n) as usize)) }
   else { let (sg, ea) = if n - 1 < 0 { ('-', 1 - n) } else { ('+', n - 1) }; if k == 1 { format!("{d}e{sg}{ea}") } else { format!("{}.{}e{sg}{ea}", &d[..1], &d[1..]) } };
  format!("{sign}{body}")
 }
 pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str { &self.0 }
}

pub struct NeutralHash(Vec<(String, Neutral)>);
impl NeutralHash {

 pub fn from_pairs(pairs: Vec<(String, Neutral)>) -> Self { let mut out: Vec<(String, Neutral)> = Vec::new(); for (k, v) in pairs { match out.iter_mut().find(|e| e.0 == k) { Some(e) => e.1 = v, None => out.push((k, v)) } } Self(out) }

 pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool { self.0.is_empty() }
 // The XML any-attribute text of each entry (Ruby to_s of a scalar); null and nested values have none.
 pub fn attribute_pairs(&self) -> Result<Vec<(String, String)>, String> {
  self.0.iter().map(|(k, v)| Ok((k.clone(), match v {
   Neutral::String(s) => s.clone(), Neutral::Bool(b) => b.to_string(),

 }
 fn nested_ok(v: &Neutral, depth: usize) -> bool { depth <= 200 && match v { Neutral::Array(a) => a.iter().all(|x| Self::nested_ok(x, depth + 1)), Neutral::Object(h) => h.0.iter().all(|e| Self::nested_ok(&e.1, depth + 1)), _ => true } }

   // f64 spellings (shortest round-trip with exponent, or plain decimal), so the source is not recoverable here;
   // the ECMAScript spelling is the only one a neutral number may have. A wire spelling is checked at parse
   // time, where it is still the source text.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct PortableFloat(f64);
impl Eq for PortableFloat {}
impl PortableFloat {
 pub fn new(v: f64) -> Result<Self, &'static str> { if v.is_finite() { Ok(Self(v)) } else { Err("non-finite float") } }
 pub fn get(&self)->f64 { self.0 }
 pub fn to_wire(self)->String {
  let x=self.0; if x==0.0 { return if x.is_sign_negative() {"-0.0".into()} else {"0.0".into()}; }
  let sci=format!("{:e}",x.abs()); let (m,e)=sci.split_once('e').unwrap(); let digits:String=m.chars().filter(|c|*c!='.').collect();
  let decpt=e.parse::<i32>().unwrap()+1; let sign=if x<0.0 {"-"} else {""};
  if decpt>-4 && decpt<=15 {
   if decpt<=0 { format!("{sign}0.{}{digits}","0".repeat(decpt.unsigned_abs() as usize)) }
   else if decpt as usize>=digits.len() { format!("{sign}{digits}{}.0","0".repeat(decpt as usize-digits.len())) }
   else { format!("{sign}{}.{}",&digits[..decpt as usize],&digits[decpt as usize..]) }
  } else { let f=if digits.len()>1 {&digits[1..]} else {"0"}; format!("{sign}{}.{f}e{}",&digits[..1],decpt-1) }
 }
 pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, &'static str> {
  let u=s.strip_prefix('-').unwrap_or(s); let (n,x)=match u.split_once('e') { Some((n,x))=>(n,Some(x)), None=>(u,None) };
  let d=|p:&str| !p.is_empty() && p.bytes().all(|c|c.is_ascii_digit());
  let ok=match n.split_once('.') { Some((w,f))=>d(w)&&d(f), None=>false } && x.is_none_or(|x|d(x.strip_prefix('-').unwrap_or(x)));
  if !ok { return Err("invalid float"); }
  match s.parse::<f64>() { Ok(v) if v.is_finite() => { let r=Self(v); if r.to_wire()==s { Ok(r) } else { Err("float is not canonical") } } _ => Err("invalid float") }
 }
}
impl Serialize for PortableFloat { fn serialize<S:serde::Serializer>(&self,s:S)->Result<S::Ok,S::Error>{ s.serialize_str(&self.to_wire()) } }
impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for PortableFloat { fn deserialize<D:serde::Deserializer<'de>>(d:D)->Result<Self,D::Error>{ Self::parse(&String::deserialize(d)?).map_err(serde::de::Error::custom) } }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(untagged, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub enum TextSource { Member { attribute: String, index: u64 }, Literal { literal: String } }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ContentToken {
 Element { attribute: String, index: u64 },
 Text { #[serde(flatten)] source: TextSource },
 Cdata { #[serde(flatten)] source: TextSource },
}
// serde cannot combine deny_unknown_fields with flatten, so tokens are read
// through one closed wire shape and then checked against the token kind.
#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct ContentTokenWire { kind: String, attribute: Option<String>, index: Option<u64>, literal: Option<String> }
impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for ContentToken {
 fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(d: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
  let w = ContentTokenWire::deserialize(d)?;
  let bad = |m: &str| serde::de::Error::custom(m);
  let source = match (w.attribute, w.index, w.literal) {
   (Some(attribute), Some(index), None) => TextSource::Member { attribute, index },
   (None, None, Some(literal)) => TextSource::Literal { literal },
   _ => return Err(bad("content token needs exactly one of attribute+index or literal")),
  };
  match (w.kind.as_str(), source) {
   ("element", TextSource::Member { attribute, index }) => Ok(Self::Element { attribute, index }),
   ("element", _) => Err(bad("element token needs attribute and index only")),
   ("text", source) => Ok(Self::Text { source }),
   ("cdata", source) => Ok(Self::Cdata { source }),
   _ => Err(bad("unknown content token kind")),
  }
 }
}
impl ContentToken {
 pub fn reference(&self) -> Option<(&str,u64)> { match self {
 Self::Element { attribute,index } | Self::Text { source: TextSource::Member { attribute,index } } | Self::Cdata { source: TextSource::Member { attribute,index } } => Some((attribute,*index)),
 _ => None,
 } }
}
